prerequisites: Elements of higher algebra and mathematical analysis (high school level)

learning_outcomes.text: Defines basic concepts from mathematical analysis, such as: distance, metric space, sphere, ball, neighborhood of a point in a metric space, particularly in the Euclidean space Rk and the real line, open/closed subset of a metric space, interior, adherent, accumulation, isolated point of a set in a metric space, bounded, compact, connected set, domain, scalar product, Euclidean norm, sequence of real numbers, monotonic sequence, bounded sequence, limit of a sequence, convergent sequence, Cauchy sequence, superior and inferior limit of a sequence, sequence in Rk, series of real numbers, convergent/divergent series, limit of a function at a point, continuous function, derivative, lateral derivative of a function at a point, critical point, local/global extreme point of a real function of one variable at a point, Taylor polynomial, Taylor formula with Peano and Lagrange remainder, Mac Laurin formula with Lagrange remainder, partial derivatives for real functions of several variables, first and second order differentials for real and vectorial functions, elements of field theory (gradient, curl, Laplacian, divergence), extreme points for real functions of several variables, primitive, Riemann integral, improper integrals, first and second kind line integrals, double integral.

States the algebraic properties of the set of real numbers and the space Rk, properties of operations with sequences that have a limit, convergence criteria for series of real numbers, properties of operations with function limits, continuous functions, differentiable functions, Fermat's, Rolle's, Cauchy's, Lagrange's theorems, their consequences and geometric interpretations, L'Hôpital's theorem, characterization of local extreme points, differentiability criterion, properties of operations with differentiable functions, characterizations of local extreme points for real functions of several real variables, properties of operations with Riemann integrable functions, integration by parts formula, Leibniz-Newton formula, variable change methods, properties of line integrals, double integrals, calculation formulas and applications of all types of studied integrals, Green's formula.
Explains and interprets theoretical and experimental results in mathematics.
Applies in complex problems the calculation formulas, theorems, and criteria mentioned above.
Operates with basic concepts, principles, and methods from mathematical analysis.
Solves mathematical problems with applicability in engineering and validates the obtained solution.

Calculates limits of sequences and functions, sums of series of real numbers, applies criteria for characterizing the convergent or divergent nature of a series of real numbers, calculates derivatives of real functions of one real variable, partial derivatives and first and second order differentials for real functions of several real variables, the Jacobian and Hessian of a function, extreme points for real functions of one, two, and three real variables, calculates integrals using integration by parts, variable changes, Euler substitutions, trigonometric substitutions, the method for calculating integrals of rational functions, calculates first kind line integrals on parametrically and explicitly given plane curves, second kind line integrals on parametrically given curves in plane and space, double integrals on rectangular domains, on simple domains with respect to the Ox, Oy axes, double integrals on disk domains by switching to polar coordinates.

Respects ethical principles, norms, and values in the correct and timely execution of professional tasks, by adopting a rigorous, efficient, and responsible work strategy in decision-making for problem-solving.
Integrates into the workgroup and applies effective relationship and work techniques in multidisciplinary teams, at various hierarchical levels.
Continuously informs and documents oneself in their field of activity by adequately using effective lifelong learning methods and techniques.

syllabus_topics: Metric spaces. Sets Rk
Sequences of real numbers
Sequences of real numbers. Sequences in Rk
Series of real numbers. Series with positive terms
Series of real numbers. Series with arbitrary terms. Absolutely convergent series
Limits of functions of one or more real variables. Continuity of functions
Differential calculus in Rk: Differentiability of real variable functions. Extreme points for functions of one real variable. Mean value theorems. Taylor's formula.
Calculus in Rk: Multivariable derivatives, partial differentials for real functions. First and second order differentials for real functions of several real variables.
Elements of field theory: gradient, divergence, curl, Laplacian. Extreme points for functions of several real variables.
Integral calculus: Definite integral (Riemann). Indefinite integral. Primitives. Integration of rational functions.
Integral calculus: Variable changes.
Integral calculus: Applications of the definite integral. Improper integrals.
First and second kind line integrals.
Double integral. Green's formula.
Topology on the set of real numbers and on Rk
Series of real numbers
Limits of real vector functions of one and several real variables
Continuity of functions. First and higher order derivatives for real functions of one real variable. Taylor's formula
Partial derivatives and first and higher order differentials for functions of several real variables
Elements of field theory. Extreme points for real functions of two and three real variables.
Primitives. Definite integrals.
Double integrals
teaching_methods: Discussions based on theoretical concepts presented on the board by the professor and digital images/sketches
Recapitulation of concepts from previous lecture
Discovery-based learning models facilitated by direct/indirect exploration of reality (demonstration, modeling)
Action-based methods such as exercise, practical activities, and problem-solving
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Whole grades from 1 to 10 will be awarded. A grade of 5 certifies the acquisition of the minimum learning outcomes for a discipline and the granting of corresponding study credits.
